text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Router LB tail latency (service=router-lb) p99 > 2.0s for 5m, streaming stalls detected, region=multi (auto-pager: @emma)

emma: on call, ack'ing. I'll page SRE.

raj: I'm up, joining. Can someone paste p95/p99 numbers and any recent deploys?

emma: p95 jumped from ~300ms to ~1.1s in last 6m. p99 ~2.2s. Streaming stall metric (streaming.stalls.total) doubled since 10:08.

kai: rolled out a routing policy change to router-lb yesterday 03:12 UTC (canary -> global rollout). commit id e3f4a1. It touched hot-shard hashing and sticky routing.

maria: customer-impact: support queue shows 6 streaming interruptions from paying customers (IDs: C-982, C-1012...). Product asked for ETA and scope.

emma: ok raj, take lead. i'll do incident comms. @kai can you confirm what the policy change did?

kai: the change modified the LB's routing algorithm to prefer low-latency zones via a policy layer. bug: it uses stale zone weights during failures which can push traffic to a hot partition in us-west-2. suspected hot partition -> queueing -> tail latency.

raj: can we get a quick snapshot of router pod latencies and connections? run: `kubectl --context=prod get pods -l app=router -o wide` and `curl -s http://router-metrics.prod.local/metrics | grep -E "p95|p99|streaming.stalls"`

emma: running commands now, pasting output:
```
$ kubectl --context=prod get pods -l app=router -n prod
NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
router-7f8d6c9b4-2kj9p        2/2     Running   0          9d
router-7f8d6c9b4-hj3xq        2/2     Running   0          9d
router-7f8d6c9b4-zl2rm        2/2     Running   0          9d
router-7f8d6c9b4-wk9pt        2/2     Running   1          2h
```

emma: metrics:
```
router_latency_p95{region="us-west-2"} 1.12
router_latency_p99{region="us-west-2"} 2.34
streaming_stalls_total{region="us-west-2"} 142
router_latency_p95{region="us-east-1"} 0.31
router_latency_p99{region="us-east-1"} 0.42
```

raj: confirms skew: us-west-2 p99 >> others. suggests hot partitioning rather than global overload. Any recent infra events in us-west-2?

kai: no infra alerts. but the policy uses a zone-weight cache updated every 60s; if an upstream healthcheck fails briefly, weights can become zero for a subpool and the policy redistributes to fewer backends — hotshard. config snippet from rollout:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  prefer_low_latency: true
  zone_weight_cache_ttl: 60s
  shard_hash: "fnv1a(user_id) % 128"
  fallback: "best_effort"
```

raj: that fallback looks suspect — "best_effort" allows concentrate. We should: 1) revert the routing policy to previous commit (v1) OR 2) patch to increase cache_ttl and enable round-robin fallback. Which is fastest?

kai: fastest is hotfix: set `fallback: round_robin` and increase `zone_weight_cache_ttl` to 300s. I can push a config roll within 3-4m. Full rollback (code) takes ~12-15m and a canary.

emma: do the hotfix. raj, coordinate rollout. I'll update incident channel and page product/support.

raj: applying patch to configmap now: `kubectl -n prod patch configmap router-config --patch '{"data":{"routing_policy":"..."}}'` (doing canary to subset of pods).

deploy-bot: starting canary rollout of config router-config -> 1/4 pods in prod (selector=router-7f8d6c9b4-wk9pt).

emma: noted. I'm posting a short blurb to #customer-notifications: "We are investigating increased tail latency affecting streaming in US-WEST-2; mitigation in progress."

kai: canary metrics after config push (1m):
```
router_latency_p95{pod="router-7f8d6c9b4-wk9pt"} 0.34
router_latency_p99{pod="router-7f8d6c9b4-wk9pt"} 0.45
streaming_stalls_total{pod="router-7f8d6c9b4-wk9pt"} 3
```

raj: good signal. rolling to remaining 3 pods with stagger 30s. monitoring p99 and stalls.

maria: product update: informing largest affected accounts, giving interim guidance (retry backoff 500ms) and offering status updates. Support ticket visibility increased.

emma: oncall handoff note: I'll stay on for comms; raj will own mitigation and post postmortem. If anything changes, ping @emma.

raj: rollout complete. post-roll metrics:
```
router_latency_p95{region="us-west-2"} 0.36
router_latency_p99{region="us-west-2"} 0.51
streaming_stalls_total{region="us-west-2"} 6 (stabilized)
```

kai: root cause summary: routing policy rollout had a fallback that concentrated traffic when zone weights were temporarily stale. This produced hot partitions in us-west-2 and increased tail latency for streaming sessions. Fix: fallback -> round_robin + longer cache TTL. Follow-ups: add unit test for fallback behavior, add more aggressive healthcheck smoothing.

emma: impact: partial degradation for streaming in US-WEST-2 for ~20m, affected small subset of customers with sticky hot keys. No data loss.

maria: opening customer incident page and scheduling postmortem with eng-sre + runtime for tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

raj: tagging incident: INC-2026-179333 (internal). I'll start the timeline and include config diffs.

emma: resolving pager. If anyone sees a regression, reopen. :white_check_mark:
